name: Zichri
overview: Zichri was a male Levite, specifically a descendant of the priestly line of Aaron, serving as a priest during the time recorded in Nehemiah. He is uniquely identified as the son of Abijah, which situates him within the Levitical priesthood responsible for temple duties and worship. His role as a priest highlights his important function in maintaining the spiritual life of Israel during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Zichri means "YHWH remembers," reflecting a theologically rich meaning that underscores God's faithfulness and remembrance of His people. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 12:17, was not given directly by God but carries significant spiritual connotation appropriate for a priestly figure.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Zichri was the son of Abijah, establishing his lineage within the Levitical priesthood. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text, limiting our knowledge of his broader family connections.
scriptureSignificance: Zichri's significance lies in his role as a priest descended from Aaron, serving during the restoration of Israel's temple worship under Nehemiah's leadership. His inclusion in the genealogical record emphasizes the continuity of the priestly line and the faithful reestablishment of worship practices after the exile. As a son of Abijah, he represents the faithful priests who helped reconstitute the spiritual life of the nation, pointing forward to the ultimate fulfillment of God's covenant through Christ.
